_readme: Proven errors in ChessVisionOFF_Puro/data/field_set.jsonl, as an OVERLAY.
The field set is the measurement, and nothing here writes to it. This file exists so a
correction can be applied at measurement time, in the open, with its evidence attached,
and so that both numbers -- as-annotated and corrected -- are always published side by
side. A correction that cannot be justified to a reader who disagrees with it does not
Bar for entry: documentary proof from the book itself, or two independent readers plus
a glyph-convention argument that can be checked from the crop. A model preferring a
different answer is NOT evidence -- that is the thing being measured.
Each entry replaces the `placement` of one annotated diagram, matched by pdf + page +
the diagram's index within that page's `diagrams` list.

evidence: The book's own move text, extracted from page 40 of the PDF with PyMuPDF, prints the
moves that follow this diagram (Stellung 58, after 32...Sh6xg4):
'33. Lf 2-d4  Tb8-b4'   -- L = Laeufer = bishop. White's bishop stands on f2.
'35. Tg7Xh7!  La6-b7'   -- black's bishop stands on a6.
Two of the three disputed squares are therefore named as bishops by the book itself.
g2 carries the same glyph as f2 and a6 -- a wide brim over a flared base -- while b3,
d5, h2, d6, g6 and h7 carry the round-headed narrow-based pawn glyph. Rendered from
the PDF at 8x and compared square by square, the two families do not overlap.
The second reader (Chess_diagram_to_FEN, an unrelated model) reads f2 and g2 as
OFFICERS too -- it says 'R' where the production model says 'B', which is its known
failure mode on this book: on Das Mittelspiel Band 1-2 p100 it turns every one of the
four bishops into a rook. It agrees they are not pawns.
Material check: with the annotation as written, White would be a knight down against
a book line that ends 'mit Figurengewinn' (winning a piece) for White. With the
correction, material is level (R+R+B+B+3P against R+R+B+N+3P).
